label: Data Movement: General Table Management
topic: Data Movement: table types, CREATE TABLE variants, Time Travel, Fail-safe and clustering keys

questions.scenario: A staging table is fully reloaded every night. TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS shows FAILSAFE_BYTES several times larger than ACTIVE_BYTES. The data can be rebuilt from the source system at any time, and the team wants to stop paying for Fail-safe storage on this table.

options.text: Run ALTER TABLE ... SET TRANSIENT to change the existing table into a transient table
Set DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 0 on the table, which also removes its Fail-safe period
Create a transient table from the data with CTAS, then replace the permanent table with it
Recreate the table as TEMPORARY, which has no Fail-safe and stays visible to other sessions

explanation.correct: A table cannot be converted to transient, so the data goes into a new transient table. Transient tables have no Fail-safe.

distractors.A: There is no way to convert a permanent table to transient in place. The conversion is not possible.
distractors.B: Fail-safe is fixed at 7 days and is not configurable. With retention 0, a dropped permanent table goes straight to Fail-safe.
distractors.D: A temporary table exists only for its session and is visible only to that session, so other sessions and jobs could not use it.

questions.scenario: On an Enterprise Edition account, ACCOUNTADMIN sets MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 5. A table in the account has DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 2, set directly on the table.
questions.stem: What is the effective Time Travel retention of the table?

options.text: 1 day, the default retention that the table's own setting replaces
2 days, the value that is set directly on the table, which wins
7 days, the retention of the table plus the Fail-safe period
5 days, the larger of the table's value and the account minimum

explanation.correct: The effective retention is the larger of DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS and MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS, so 5 days.

distractors.A: 1 day is the default retention. The table has its own setting, and the account minimum is higher.
distractors.B: The table's own value is lower than the account minimum, so the minimum applies.
distractors.C: Fail-safe is separate from Time Travel and is not added to the retention.

questions.scenario: A source table has a clustering key, and Automatic Clustering is suspended on it. A Data Engineer creates three copies for testing: one with CLONE, one with LIKE and one with CTAS that includes CLUSTER BY.
questions.stem: Which statement about the copies is correct?

options.text: The clone keeps the clustering key, and Automatic Clustering starts out resumed on the clone
The LIKE table keeps the clustering key, and its Automatic Clustering is not suspended
The CTAS table with CLUSTER BY starts with Automatic Clustering suspended, as on the source
The LIKE table loses the clustering key because it copies only column definitions

explanation.correct: A LIKE copy keeps the source's clustering keys, and Automatic Clustering is not suspended by default, even if it was suspended on the source.

distractors.A: A clone keeps the clustering key, but Automatic Clustering is suspended by default on the clone.
distractors.C: A CTAS with clustering keys enables Automatic Clustering by default, even if it was suspended on the source.
distractors.D: A LIKE copy keeps the source's clustering keys.

questions.scenario: A Data Engineer uses CREATE OR ALTER TABLE to rename the column cust_nm to customer_name by changing it in the table definition. The column holds data in every row.
questions.stem: What happens to the data in that column?

options.text: The old column is dropped and a new one is added, so the data in that column is lost
The column is renamed in place and keeps its data, because the type and position match
The column is renamed and the data is kept only if the definition adds a CLONE clause
The statement fails because CREATE OR ALTER TABLE cannot change the names of columns

explanation.correct: With CREATE OR ALTER TABLE, a rename is a drop plus an add, so the data in that column is lost.

distractors.B: There is no in-place rename. CREATE OR ALTER TABLE treats a changed name as a drop and an add.
distractors.C: CLONE is not supported inside CREATE OR ALTER TABLE, and it would not carry the data over.
distractors.D: The statement runs. The result is a dropped column and a new one.

questions.scenario: A Data Engineer reviews how Time Travel and Fail-safe behave on permanent tables in an Enterprise Edition account before documenting the recovery process for a team.
questions.stem: Which THREE statements are correct? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Transient tables keep a 7-day Fail-safe period that Snowflake can recover from
Fail-safe lasts 7 days, cannot be changed, and only Snowflake can recover from it
A query that uses AT or BEFORE sees the table schema as it was at that earlier time
With retention set to 0, a dropped permanent table goes straight to Fail-safe
ACCOUNTADMIN can turn Time Travel off for the account as a whole for every object
UNDROP fails if an object with the same name already exists in the schema

explanation.correct: Fail-safe is 7 days, not configurable, and recoverable only by Snowflake. With retention 0, a dropped permanent table goes straight to Fail-safe. UNDROP fails if an object with the same name exists, so the existing one must be renamed first.

distractors.C: A query that uses AT or BEFORE uses the current table schema, not the earlier one.
distractors.E: Time Travel cannot be turned off for an account as a whole. ACCOUNTADMIN can set the account value to 0, which changes only the default for new objects, and any database, schema or table can override it.
